q: Which Italian artist painted the Mona Lisa?
note: The painting became a worldwide celebrity partly because it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 and missing for two years.

q: Which Dutch post-Impressionist painted The Starry Night?
note: He painted the swirling night sky from a window of the asylum at Saint-Rémy, from memory rather than direct observation.

q: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
note: He considered himself a sculptor rather than a painter and took the commission reluctantly, spending four years on the scaffold.

q: Which Spanish artist painted Guernica and helped invent Cubism?
note: Guernica was his response to the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War in 1937.

q: In which Paris museum does the Mona Lisa hang?
note: The building was a royal palace long before it became a museum, opening to the public after the French Revolution.

q: Which Norwegian artist painted The Scream?
note: He made several versions of the image, and two of them have been stolen and later recovered.

q: Which French sculptor created the bronze figure known as The Thinker?
note: The figure began as a small part of a much larger doorway sculpture, The Gates of Hell.

q: Which Spanish Surrealist painted The Persistence of Memory, with its drooping melted watches?
note: He said the soft watches were inspired by a wheel of Camembert melting in the sun.

q: Which French painter's canvas Impression, Sunrise gave the Impressionist movement its name?
note: A hostile critic coined the word "Impressionists" as an insult, and the painters cheerfully adopted it.

q: Which Mexican painter is known for unflinching self-portraits and the double portrait The Two Fridas?
note: She began painting seriously while bedridden after a streetcar accident, using a mirror mounted above her bed.

q: Which American artist painted Nighthawks, showing four figures in a late-night diner?
note: There is no visible door into the diner, which is part of why the scene feels so sealed off.

q: Which Dutch master painted the enormous militia group portrait known as The Night Watch?
note: Its familiar nickname comes from centuries of darkened varnish; the scene is actually set in daylight.

q: Which artist made the Pop Art silkscreens of Campbell's Soup Cans and Marilyn Monroe?
note: He began as a successful commercial illustrator, which is exactly why the art world was slow to take him seriously.

q: Which Italian Renaissance artist painted The Birth of Venus, showing the goddess arriving on a scallop shell?
note: It hangs in the Uffizi in Florence, painted for the Medici circle at the height of their power.

q: What is the title of Grant Wood's painting of a stern farmer holding a pitchfork beside a woman, in front of a white farmhouse?
note: The title refers to the pointed window on the house behind them, a style called Carpenter Gothic.

q: Which famous armless ancient Greek statue of Aphrodite is named after the island where it was found?
note: A farmer uncovered it on Milos in 1820, and nobody knows what the missing arms were doing.

q: Which Dutch painter created Girl with a Pearl Earring?
note: Only about three dozen paintings are firmly attributed to him, and he was largely forgotten for two centuries.

q: Which Spanish painter put himself at his easel in the royal group portrait Las Meninas?
note: The king and queen appear only as a small reflection in a mirror at the back of the room.

q: Which Japanese artist made the woodblock print The Great Wave off Kanagawa?
note: It is one sheet from his series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, and the mountain sits small behind the wave.

q: Which Netherlandish painter created the crowded, nightmarish triptych The Garden of Earthly Delights?
note: One damned figure in the hell panel has musical notation written across his backside, which modern musicians have transcribed and played.
